chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The leper (al-barsha'), the insane woman (al-majnounah), and the leper (al-majdhumah) are returned [in marriage]." I asked, "The one-eyed woman?" He said, "No."

key_terms.الْبَرْصَاءُ: The leper (specifically referring to leprosy or a specific skin disease)
key_terms.الْعَوْرَاءُ: The one-eyed woman (or woman with a visual defect)
key_terms.الْمَجْذُومَةُ: The leper (often distinguished from al-barsha' in medical jurisprudence)
key_terms.الْمَجْنُونَةُ: The insane woman (referring to mental instability)

ai.seo_question: Which physical or mental defects cause a marriage to be returned in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *al-Tadlis* (concealment of defects) in marriage, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that severe contagious diseases like leprosy (*al-Barasa'* and *al-Majdhuma*) and insanity (*al-Majnouna*) are grounds for annulment due to their impact on marital life and health. The Imam’s specific negation regarding the one-eyed woman (*al-Awrā’*) highlights the juristic distinction between conditions that significantly impair marital companionship versus those that are merely cosmetic or minor, a nuance central to Shia fiqh on marriage validity.
